dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the unfiltered fetch on cache HITS (resolve_ref blobless=False before the dest.is_dir() check) is an acceptable cost, or gate the unfiltered fetch on an actual cache miss.
evidence: cache.py:180 `sha = resolve_ref(ref, repo_root, fetch=fetch, blobless=False)` runs before the cache check at cache.py:184 `if dest.is_dir():`
resolve_ref with fetch=True + remote calls `_fetch_origin(root, remote=remote, blobless=blobless)` (repo_snapshot.py:417-418), and blobless=False selects `--no-filter` (repo_snapshot.py:356)
DEFAULT_REF is a MOVING ref: `DEFAULT_REF = "origin/main"` (repo_snapshot.py:91), so the general fetch cannot be skipped on cache hits — the SHA is unknown until after the fetch
repo_snapshot.py:646 `sha = resolve_ref(ref, repo_root, fetch=fetch, blobless=False)` similarly precedes the `if dest.is_dir():` cache hit at repo_snapshot.py:649
dropped.finding: resolve_ref(..., blobless=False) is invoked unconditionally before the cache-hit check, so on a cache HIT (SHA already materialized, nothing to materialize) the resolution now runs a full unfiltered `git fetch --no-filter <remote>` instead of the prior `--filter=blob:none`. For the default moving ref origin/main, every acquire()/materialize() with fetch=True pays a whole-remote blob transfer on the hot cache-hit path.
scenarios: Long-lived MCP server repeatedly acquiring origin/main where the tip SHA is already in the content-addressed store
CI lane that re-materializes an already-cached SHA but with fetch=True

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the `_GIT_TIMEOUT` constant assertion with a behavioral test that a stuck git invocation on the materialize path is bounded (e.g. monkeypatch `run_git`/`subprocess.run` to raise `TimeoutExpired` and assert the call returns/raises promptly rather than blocking).
evidence: Rule-4 refactoring violation: the test breaks if `_GIT_TIMEOUT` is renamed even with no behavior change; Rule-4 regression-blindness: it still passes if `timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT` were dropped from `subprocess.run`/`run_git` (repo_snapshot.py:302, 372, 542), which is the precise hang the fix prevents.
Ticket 747f AC(2): 'no run_git call on the materialize path can block indefinitely (timeout or GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH), asserted by test' — this assertion on a bare constant does not satisfy that AC.
dropped.finding: `test_snapshot_git_calls_are_time_bounded` asserts only that the internal constant `rs._GIT_TIMEOUT` is a positive number; it does not assert the timeout is wired into any subprocess call, so it is a change-detector on an internal name that is blind to the exact regression the ticket targets (a git call blocking indefinitely).
scenarios: A refactor moves the timeout to a per-call literal and drops the constant → test breaks though behavior is unchanged.
A regression removes `timeout=` from a subprocess call on the materialize path → test still passes.
